body:
The math release. LaTeX formulas render natively in the preview — no WebKit, no JavaScript — and in titles, the outline and the breadcrumb. Around it: preview zoom and line spacing, a default view for files opened from outside, lists that continue on Enter, and formatting shortcuts. Linux packages build again on Swift 6.4.

## Features

- **LaTeX math** (#37, #62) — `$…$` inline and `$$…$$` or a ` ```math ` fence as a centred display block, drawn by [RaTeX](https://github.com/erweixin/RaTeX) 0.1.15 (Rust, MIT; KaTeX fonts under the OFL) through a C bridge in its own `MathEngine` target. Inline formulas are Pango shapes inside the existing labels: they sit on the baseline, wrap like words, follow the text colour and the zoom, copy as `$tex$` and read as TeX to screen readers. `align*`, matrices, `cases`, `\ce{}`, `\tag`, `\color` and `\newcommand` work; a formula that does not parse shows its source.
- **Formulas outside the preview** — note titles and headings in the sidebar, outline, breadcrumb, filtered rows and command palette draw them too, parsed on a shared time budget so a long list never stalls the window.
- **Preview zoom and line spacing** (#36) — Ctrl+scroll zooms in 10 % steps from 50 % to 200 %; Settings → Preview gains *Preview zoom* and *Line spacing* (80–200 %), applied live in every window. Images keep their size, code blocks their own spacing.
- **The view opened files start in** (#35) — Settings → Editor → *Opened files start in*: Editor, Split or Preview. Split stays the default; windows already open are left alone.
- **Lists, quotes and tables continue on Enter** (#34) — bullets keep marker and indent, ordered items count up, checked tasks continue unchecked, quotes continue with `> `, a table row gets an empty sibling. Enter on an empty item ends it; Shift+Enter stays inside the item.
- **Formatting shortcuts** (#33) — Ctrl+B bold, Ctrl+I italic, Ctrl+K link, Ctrl+E code, Ctrl+Shift+Q quote, Ctrl+Shift+L bulleted list, Ctrl+Shift+O numbered list, in the library and in opened files. All letters on purpose: GTK never fires a `<Shift>`+digit accelerator.

## Fixes

- **A note holding a NUL opened empty** — GtkTextBuffer refuses such text whole, and the next keystroke saved the empty buffer over the note. A NUL now shows, and is saved, as U+FFFD.
- **The split preview lost its width beside the Outline** — one `PreviewPaneDivider` now drives both windows; the stored preview width no longer counts the Outline (`workspace.json` is migrated once), and toggling a sidebar or the Outline in Editor mode no longer shifts the divider when the preview comes back. Sizes read from a damaged `workspace.json` are clamped.
- **Titles with `<` or `&` broke toasts and the banner** — both show plain text now (`Toast.plain`), and Pango markup is escaped per code point everywhere.
- **The snap could not start** — the GNOME 46 platform ships no libspelling; the snap now stages its own. Launchpad builds also failed outright for lack of `msgfmt` (gettext was never a build-package).
- **libspelling 0.2 CRITICALs** — Ubuntu 24.04's libspelling returns the language list as a `GPtrArray`, not a `GListModel`; every Settings window corrupted memory on it.
- **Linux release packages failed to build on Swift 6.4** — SwiftPM 6.4's default build system does not link a static Foundation's dependencies; the static build uses the native build system.

## Packaging

- **Building needs Rust 1.88+** and `scripts/build-ratex-bridge.sh` before the first `swift build`. Every package builds it: deb, rpm, AppImage and snap through `assemble-install-root.sh`, Flatpak with the rust-stable SDK extension and offline crates (`flatpak/ratex-cargo-sources.json`, checked against `Cargo.lock` in CI), macOS with rustup pinned to 1.91.
- Linux packages are built with Swift 6.4; the snap downloads 6.4.0.
- **The Flatpak moves to GNOME 51** (Freedesktop 26.08: GTK 4.24, libadwaita 1.10), so it too builds with Swift 6.4 — 6.4.1 from the 26.08 Swift extension, where GNOME 50's was 6.3.3. The bundled libspelling stays at its latest tag, 0.4.10: the GNOME 51 SDK still has none.
- The AppImage runtime moves to the type2-runtime build of 2026-10-19 (extraction directories created with mode 0700), pinned by checksum as before.

## Robustness

- Every bridge entry point catches panics; TeX length, nesting, layout boxes and emoji per formula are bounded; NaN/∞ boxes are rejected.
- Parsing runs on time budgets with an LRU cache; postponed formulas are laid out on the following frames.
- What formulas cost to draw is bounded per label (128 MiB) and for the whole preview (1 GiB): GTK draws every Pango shape into a node the size of its whole label.
- Text missing from the math fonts (Cyrillic, Greek) is drawn with a serif system font chosen through fontconfig.

## Testing and CI

- CI's core suites are listed once, in `scripts/core-test-suites.txt`, for CI and the release check, which now also runs the preview widget suites. The engine's tests are their own `MathEngineTests` target.
- CI installs colour emoji and pins the engine's fallback font, so the emoji-limit tests run instead of skipping themselves.
- macOS builds on Xcode 26.4.1 (what releases use) and on the Xcode 27 image, and CI builds the Release `.app` the DMG ships.
- The UI smoke harness never deletes through a mount in its runtime directory: a session's document portal mounts real folders there.
- `actions/cache` and `action-gh-release` move to their Node 24 releases.

## Also

- The software-centre description catches up with the app — formulas, the outline with find and replace, formatting shortcuts and lists that continue on Enter, preview zoom — and the AppStream and desktop keywords gain *math* and *LaTeX*. It and the 1.6.0 release notes are translated into all thirteen languages.
- Depends on swift-adwaita 2.0.2.

---

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/makoni/swifty-notes-gtk/compare/1.5.0...1.6.0

The localization release. Thirteen languages besides English, switchable from Settings without a restart, with right-to-left layout for Arabic and Hebrew. One gettext catalogue per language covers the interface, the CLI, the desktop entry and the store listing. Plus a fifth Linux package: AppImage.

## Features

- **Thirteen languages** (#32, #38) — Arabic, German, Spanish, French, Hebrew, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Dutch, Brazilian Portuguese, Russian, Simplified and Traditional Chinese. 412 entries each, no fuzzies, `msgcmp` clean. `po/LINGUAS` is the single list that drives catalogue compilation and the desktop/metainfo merge alike.
- **Language picker** — applied live through gettext's cache invalidation, not at startup. `system` follows the session; every other row pins. Rows are ordered by the name each one shows.
- **Right-to-left layout** — the app assigns GTK's default direction itself rather than letting `gtk_init` derive it from GTK's own catalogue, which is what lets the direction follow the picker. Sidebar and outline swap sides; switching back restores the original coordinates.
- **Translation contexts** (#40) — `msgctxt`, so one msgid can serve two roles.
- Traditional Chinese is a translation, not a script conversion: 387 of its 412 strings differ from the simplified catalogue, mostly vocabulary (資料夾/文件夹, 檔案/文件, 儲存/保存, 設定/设置). gettext does not fall back from `zh_TW` to `zh_CN`, so without it a Taiwanese session saw English.

## Packaging

- **AppImage** joins deb, rpm, Flatpak and Snap, per architecture, from the same `/usr` install root the deb and rpm builds consume. Runtime is `AppImage/type2-runtime` at `continuous`, pinned by sha256: static-pie with libfuse linked in, so it needs only a `fusermount` on `$PATH` rather than the `libfuse.so.2` current distributions stopped shipping.
- **In-place updates.** Each AppImage embeds `gh-releases-zsync|…` and publishes a `.zsync` delta. The Update button hands the bundle to `appimageupdatetool` or `AppImageUpdate` when `APPIMAGE` names a readable file and one is on `$PATH`; otherwise, and on every other install kind, it opens the release page as before.
- **An AppImage is not a sandbox** — unlike Flatpak and Snap it is unconfined, and the problem is the mirror image: the bundle mounts at a fresh directory each launch, so absolute paths compiled into dependencies point at the host. The launcher is redirected with `SWIFTY_NOTES_ROOT_PREFIX`, and the 20 hunspell dictionaries the Flatpak ships reach enchant through `XDG_DATA_DIRS`. Enchant's *provider* modules cannot be redirected, so **spell check needs `enchant-2` on the host** and is silently unavailable without it. See `docs/APPIMAGE.md`.
- The AppImage build is its own `workflow_call` / `workflow_dispatch` workflow, so the path can be exercised without drafting a release.

## Fixes

- **The language picker did nothing under a C locale** (#46) — GLib decides once per process whether the program is translated, and decides "no" when the first lookup runs under a locale that neither equals `C` nor begins with `en_` with no catalogue loaded. `C.UTF-8` is exactly that gap, and GTK makes that lookup itself. Affected Flatpak sandboxes, containers and CI runners.
- **System-language dates were always English** (#47) — corelibs `Locale.current` answers `en_001` on Linux whatever the environment says. `interfaceLocale()` now resolves from the pinned language, then `LC_TIME`, then a normalized `LANGUAGE`.
- **Renaming the seeded showcase note stranded its image** (#56) — the repair keyed off the literal title, which is just the note's first heading. It keys off the asset link now.
- **`swift build -c release` did not compile**, and had not since #31: a `#if DEBUG`-only helper was called from an ungated launch hook. CI builds release as well as debug now.
- The macOS test bundle stopped building (#45).

## Testing

- Catalogue guards are parameterized over `po/LINGUAS` (#41, #44), so adding a language extends the coverage by itself: fuzzies, empty translations, format-specifier parity, plural-form count, `.mo` against `.po`, packaging metadata.
- The countless-plural guard reads each catalogue's own `plural=` expression instead of assuming `msgstr[0]` is the singular — Arabic's form 0 is the *zero* form, so the old rule failed a correct Arabic catalogue.
- Live language switching under headless Wayland: English → Arabic → English in one process, pane geometry measured at each stage and asserted back to the same coordinates.
- Every shipped language reaches its own catalogue — 13 cases comparing three labels against the `.po` on disk, which catches `zh_TW` resolving to `zh_CN`.
- CI runs on every pull request in both repos, not only on pushes to the default branch.

## Also

- Seeded note content deliberately stays English (#39): it is content rather than chrome, and translating it would make first launch decide once and permanently which language a user's *files* are in.
- The release notes shown in your software centre are themselves translated for the first time, in all thirteen languages.
- Depends on swift-adwaita 1.6.0.

---

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/makoni/swifty-notes-gtk/compare/1.4.0...1.5.0

This release brings the Outline panel and Find & Replace to Markdown files opened directly from the file manager — for everyone who uses Swifty Notes as a standalone .md editor, no notes library required. ## Features - Outline, quick jump, and Find & Replace in directly opened files (#25) — F9 toggles the document Outline with click-to-jump and scroll tracking, Ctrl+G opens the quick-jump palette, Ctrl+F searches the editor or the preview, and Ctrl+H replaces in the editor. Collapsing an Outline section folds it in the editor, and the Outline preferences from Settings apply here too. Shortcuts route to whichever window is focused, so the notes library keeps working exactly as before. ## Fixes - pressing Ctrl+F with a selection no longer prefills the search field with the wrong characters when emoji or flags appear before the selection (affected the notes library too). - opening a Markdown file directly now populates the Outline immediately instead of waiting for the first edit. **Full Changelog**: https://github.com/makoni/swifty-notes-gtk/compare/1.3.0...1.4.0

This release renders GitHub-style emoji shortcodes in the preview and cleans up the update checker for sandboxed installs. ## Features - emoji shortcodes render in the preview (#28) — `:white_check_mark:` becomes ✅, `:rocket:` becomes 🚀, using the same gemoji vocabulary as GitHub (1913 shortcodes). Works in headings, paragraphs, lists, quotes, tables, and link labels; code spans, code blocks, and URLs stay literal, and the Markdown source on disk is never changed. Glyphs come from the system color-emoji font, and a new Settings → Preview toggle turns the substitution off. ## Fixes - "Check for Updates…" no longer appears in Flatpak/Snap installs without network access, where it could only ever fail with a raw network error — store installs get update notifications from the store itself. Host installs (.deb/.rpm) that are merely offline at launch keep the entry. - a manual update check that fails offline now shows a friendly "no internet connection" message instead of the raw error text, and stays retryable. **Full Changelog**: https://github.com/makoni/swifty-notes-gtk/compare/1.2.0...1.3.0

This release adds an Outline navigation panel, in-document Find & Replace, and live search highlighting in the preview — the biggest editing-workflow update since 1.0, aimed at navigating and editing long Markdown notes. ## Features - **Outline navigation panel (#25)** — a toggleable side panel (F9) listing every heading in the note, with scroll-spy that tracks your position, a breadcrumb of the current section, heading filter/search, collapsible sections, fold-in-editor via the chevron, drag-to-reorder of whole sections, H4–H6 visual hierarchy, and per-note persistence of collapse state and recent jumps. A Ctrl+G command palette gives quick-jump to any heading. - **Find & Replace (#26)** — Ctrl+F to find, Ctrl+H to replace, with Replace / Replace All, case-sensitive and regex matching (including backreferences), match counts, query memory, and smooth-scroll to each hit. Search routes to the focused pane in split mode and works in both the editor and the live preview. - **Search highlighting in the preview (#27)** — matches highlight directly in the rendered preview through a Pango attribute overlay, including inside fenced code blocks and table cells, with a distinct active-match style. ## Fixes - Ctrl+F in preview-only mode now searches the visible preview instead of the hidden editor (#27). - preview-only mode no longer briefly shows the editor when switching into it. - search highlights are cleared correctly when the query changes or the preview re-renders, so stale highlights no longer linger. - Ctrl+G command palette regression fixed — backdrop click and Escape dismiss it again, and search keeps focus during incremental filtering. - outline scroll-spy no longer fights click-driven scroll animations or mis-maps headings in grouped layouts. - resetting the notes directory back to the default no longer wipes the outline panel preferences. ## Performance - preview rendering coalesces flat and nested lists, table cells, and heading + trailing paragraphs into single Pango labels, cutting widget count and keeping long notes responsive while scrolling. - outline panel stops rebuilding rows on every scroll-spy tick, collapses the breadcrumb to a single label, and memoizes the active-heading refresh. ## Internal - adopt swift-adwaita wrappers across the app — URIScheme allowlist, PangoMarkup.escape, Label.attributes for highlights, and replacing raw GTK C calls; swift-adwaita pin bumped to 1.5.0. - isolated deinit for the scroll-spy driver, dedup of the searchable-text helper against the search engine, and a new profiling guide (docs/PROFILING.md). **Full Changelog**: https://github.com/makoni/swifty-notes-gtk/compare/1.1.7...1.2.0

This release adds native macOS support alongside the existing Linux packages and introduces an in-app update notification when a newer GitHub release is published. ## Native macOS build Swifty Notes now ships a signed, notarized, and stapled `.dmg` for Apple Silicon (macOS 26.0+) alongside the Linux packages. Drag-and-drop install, run, and the GTK/libadwaita app behaves like a native Cocoa application. **Packaging & distribution** - Signed/notarized/stapled `.dmg` produced by the release pipeline (`release-packages` workflow), with the macOS Xcode project also exercised in CI. - Bundled Homebrew GTK4 / libadwaita / libspelling / gtksourceview / pango / harfbuzz / gdk-pixbuf / graphene / cairo / intl dylibs and GTK resources inside the `.app`, so the app runs without a separate Homebrew prereq. - `MARKETING_VERSION` from the release pipeline is plumbed through `xcodebuild` and `Info.plist`, so the About dialog and `--version` agree with the release tag. **Native Cocoa polish** - Traffic lights now live in the main toolbar — the sidebar's `AdwHeaderBar` was dropped on macOS so the window-control buttons land in the right place. - `Cmd+Q` quits via an app-level `GAction`, which also lights up the standard "Quit Swifty Notes" item in the Apple menu. - Hamburger menu uses a custom popover on macOS (GMenu doesn't bridge to NSMenu under GTK's macOS backend); Linux keeps the native GMenu. - About-dialog icon path fixed for the macOS bundle layout. - Reliable single-click on sidebar rows and context menus. - Click handling unified through a `MacOSClickWorkaround` for buttons across the app (formatting toolbar, settings, update banner, etc.) — works around GTK's macOS backend swallowing click events on some widgets. Dual-path handler with 200 ms dedup avoids the double-fire regression. - Drag-to-folder restored after a CLAIM-based gesture regression. - Live theme refresh for bundled SVG icons (formatting toolbar, view-mode toggles, sort icons) on light/dark switches. - View-mode + sort + toolbar icons rebundled to work around a `GtkSymbolicPaintable` ``-element parsing regression on macOS. - Brew share dirs merged into `XDG_DATA_DIRS` for `swift run` developer launches so GSettings schemas resolve. - Brew icon-theme symlinks dereferenced when bundling so the `.app` ships real files. ## In-app update notification Swifty Notes now lets you know when a newer release is available. - A friendly banner appears at the top of the editor with an **Update** button (opens the GitHub release page) and a dismiss button. - A new **Check for Updates…** entry in the main menu runs the check on demand and surfaces a toast for the up-to-date and error outcomes. - The check hits `api.github.com/repos/makoni/swifty-notes-gtk/releases/latest` with a 10s timeout and compares semantic versions against the running build. `BuildInfo.version` resolution order: `SWIFTY_NOTES_VERSION` env override → `CFBundleShortVersionString` from the macOS bundle → built-in default. - A `--force-update-available` launch flag surfaces the banner even when you're already on the latest release — handy for QA without shipping a new tag. - Linux fix: launch-time check uses `Task.detached` and dispatches the completion via `MainContext.idle`. A MainActor-isolated `Task { … }` would never start its body, because GTK blocks the main thread inside `g_main_loop_run` and Swift's MainActor executor never gets pumped — macOS hides this because Cocoa's run loop and GLib loop share the main thread. The completion is built as a `@MainActor @Sendable` closure so Swift 6 strict concurrency doesn't flag the cross-isolation send of `self`. ## Bug fixes - **Open Markdown File for paths containing spaces (#24).** Opening standalone files from outside the library — including from the file manager's Open With flow — works reliably again when the path contains a space, such as notes stored under "My Documents" or a cloud-synced folder like "Cloud Disk". This finished the migration to `URL.path(percentEncoded: false)` across the remaining call sites; integration tests now cover those paths. - **Syntax highlighting for `bash` and `csharp` code blocks.** Fenced code blocks tagged with those language ids now resolve to their actual `GtkSourceView` languages in the preview, matching the other supported languages. ## Tests & CI - Integration coverage for the update-check pipeline on both macOS and Linux (banner reveal, toast on up-to-date / error, force-flag promotion, action wiring). - Coverage for spaces-in-path call sites touched by the `.path` migration. - macOS DMG build orchestrated inside the `release-packages` workflow; `release-macos` codesign step hardened (drop deprecated `--deep`, install `adwaita-icon-theme` alongside the other Homebrew deps, state dumps to isolate failures). **Full Changelog**: https://github.com/makoni/swifty-notes-gtk/compare/1.1.6...1.1.7

## Highlights - Typing and preview updates are significantly more efficient on long Markdown notes. - Preview refresh work now waits for typing bursts instead of rebuilding on every keystroke. - The preview reuses more existing widgets and rendered blocks, which reduces redraw churn and makes editing feel steadier. - Sidebar updates now avoid unnecessary rerenders during body-only edits. - Performance work was profiled across mixed-content notes and long text-heavy notes, with targeted wins for both paths. - Regression coverage was expanded for typing bursts, preview reuse, incremental preview building, and stacked preview row reuse. ## Technical details - Typing-driven preview refreshes now defer Markdown block building until the debounce boundary instead of rebuilding on every editor change. - `MarkdownPreview` now updates custom-text labels in place instead of rebuilding that subtree. - `MainWindow` now skips sidebar refreshes during body-only edits unless the derived title or active search results actually change. - Added `IncrementalPreviewBlockBuilder` for conservative incremental block rebuilding on safe text-only documents, with full-render fallback for unsupported Markdown structures. - Stacked preview rows for headings, paragraph runs, and blockquote runs are now updated in place when the row kind stays compatible. - Widget-level and window-level regression tests were added for deferred typing refresh, sidebar fast paths, incremental preview rebuilding, custom-text reuse, and stacked row reuse. ## Measured results - Mixed-content typing workload: sidebar refresh removal reduced sampled event count by about 33.6%. - Long text-heavy typing workload: incremental preview building reduced sampled event count by about 12.9%, and preview block building dropped from a visible hotspot to a minor cost. - Stacked preview text-row reuse delivered an additional measured improvement of about 3.3% on the targeted workload. **Full Changelog**: https://github.com/makoni/swifty-notes-gtk/compare/1.1.5...1.1.6

This release closes eight issues with a heavy focus on note safety (Trash + restore), smarter paste, and Markdown rendering polish. ## Trash & restore (#17) Deleting a note is now a soft-delete that lands in a sidebar Trash section instead of erasing the file. The bin is always visible at the bottom of the sidebar with a count badge. **GUI** - Right-click a trashed note for **Restore** / **Delete forever** (with confirmation). - Right-click the Trash header for **Empty Trash** (with confirmation). - Every soft-delete shows a toast with **Undo** that restores the note in one click. - Trashed notes open in a strict read-only preview: banner + dimmed editor + disabled formatting toolbar + autosave cancelled. Multiple guards protect against keystroke / paste / drag-drop / preview-checkbox / formatting-toolbar / autosave-timer / external-reload writes leaking into the wrong note. - Folder delete now routes nested notes through Trash too — folder deletion is no longer the one path that destroys notes permanently. Restore reconstructs the original sub-folder tree on demand. - Trash expansion state persists across launches (`WorkspaceState.isTrashExpanded`). **Settings** - New "Empty Trash automatically" preference in Settings → Storage. Options: Never / 7 / 30 / 90 / 365 days. Default 30. The retention sweep runs at app launch; legacy entries without a timestamp get stamped on first encounter so the next sweep ages them out. **Storage internals** - Trashed notes live in `notes/.trash//` with `deletedAt` + `originalFolderPath` in `meta.json`. The dot-prefix keeps `loadNotes` skipping the directory via `.skipsHiddenFiles`. - `NotesRepository` gained `moveToTrash` / `trashedNotes` / `restore` / `permanentlyDelete` / `emptyTrash` / `pruneTrashIfNeeded`. - `TrashRetention` enum (`.never` / `.days(Int)`, Codable) added to `AppSettings`. ## Auto-wrap pasted URLs as Markdown links (#19) Pasting a bare http/https URL now inserts a Markdown link automatically. - No selection → `[https://x](https://x)`. - With selection → `[selection](https://x)`. - Inside a fenced or inline code span → falls through to plain paste (URLs stay raw, since Markdown doesn't render link syntax in code regions). - Non-URL text → falls through unchanged. - URL detection rejects empty hosts, internal whitespace, and non-http schemes (`javascript:`, `mailto:`, `file:`, `ftp:`) up front so the auto-wrap can't be turned into an XSS-style smuggle. Helper logic lives in `Services/MarkdownLinkPaste.swift` (16 unit tests + 4 integration tests). ## Paste images & file-manager copies (#15) Ctrl+V on a clipboard image, or pasting files copied from a file manager, now imports them into the active note's `assets/` folder and inserts a `![](path)` reference — same code path as drag-and-drop. - `MainWindow.importPastedImage(pngData:)` bridges clipboard PNG bytes to the editor. - `NotesRepository.importImageAsset(data:baseName:fileExtension:for:)` accepts raw bytes, not just URLs. ## Task-list checkboxes are clickable in preview (#18) - Click a `☐` / `☑` in the preview to toggle the matching `[ ]` / `[x]` line in the editor; saved automatically. - Loose lists (items separated by blank lines) now render with paragraph-style spacing **per item** instead of per-list. - Ordered lists restart numbering when the author writes a fresh ordinal after a blank line (CommonMark-correct). ## Markdown rendering polish (#16, #22) - Standalone image lines render as full-width block images instead of inline (`smart-B` paragraph splitting). - Sentence-internal images stay inline; image-only lines get promoted to plain block images while image cards stay loose. - Block images correctly resize when the preview pane is widened after open. - Badge rows keep their requested size in image groups. - List rows got a small symmetric vertical breather; trailing newline stripped from item text so rows don't grow an empty second line. ## Folder name validation (#20) - The New Folder dialog now treats `/` as a nesting separator (`a/b/c` creates intermediates). - Hidden names (leading dot), whitespace-only names, and Windows-incompatible names are rejected with a clear error message. ## Flatpak: 21 bundled hunspell dictionaries (#23) The Flatpak build now ships with hunspell dictionaries for **en, de, es, fr, it, pl, ru, uk, cs, da, nl, fi, hu, nb, pt, ro, sk, sl, sr, sv, he**, so inline spell-check works out of the box for those languages without installing extra packages. CI smoke-tests verify the dictionaries are present in the built Flatpak. **Full Changelog**: https://github.com/makoni/swifty-notes-gtk/compare/1.1.4...1.1.5

Two big features land in this release: ## Folders (#10) Notes can now live in folders. Folders are real directories under the notes root, with arbitrary nesting (limited only by the file system), so syncing through Syncthing / Nextcloud / Dropbox / Git keeps working unchanged. **GUI** - Sidebar tree with expand/collapse — open state persists across launches via `WorkspaceState.expandedFolders`. - "+ folder" button in the header creates root-level folders. - Folder context menu: New note here, New subfolder…, Rename folder…, Delete folder… - Note context menu gains "Move to…" with a folder picker. - Drag-and-drop in the sidebar: - drag note → folder, or folder → folder - hover over a closed folder for ~500 ms during a drag and it auto-expands - rejects self-drop and folder-into-descendant - Dialogs polished: Create/Rename disabled until the typed name is non-empty (and different from the current name for rename), Enter submits. **CLI parity** (drop-in for scripts and AI agents): - `swiftynotes cli list --folder PATH` — scope the list to a folder and its descendants - `swiftynotes cli folders` — JSON array of every folder path - `swiftynotes cli folders create ` - `swiftynotes cli folders rm [-y|--yes]` — apt-style; refuses to wipe non-empty folders without `--yes` - `swiftynotes cli folders rename ` - `swiftynotes cli folders move --to ` - `swiftynotes cli create --content '...' --folder Work/Drafts` — intermediate folders auto-created - `swiftynotes cli move --folder Personal` (`--folder ""` to move to root) **Storage internals** - `Note.folderPath` (relative slash-separated, `""` = root) threaded through the model. - `NotesRepository` walker treats `/note.md` directories as leaves; everything else under the notes root is a folder. - Folder-name validation against `pathconf(_PC_NAME_MAX)` and full-path validation against `_PC_PATH_MAX`, with conservative fallbacks. - `cannotNestInsideNote` error guards against creating folders/notes inside a `/` directory (closes a CLI escape hatch). - Duplicate-id resolver: cloning a UUID directory across folders produces two notes with the same `id`; the resolver mints a fresh UUID for the later occurrence and rewrites its `meta.json` so reloads are stable. - `directorySnapshot` filenames now include the folder path so cross-folder collisions surface in change detection. ## Spell-check (#14) Inline misspelling underlines via libspelling-1, integrated as a SwiftPM `systemLibrary` target. - Right-click a misspelled word for suggestions, Add to Dictionary, or Ignore. - Language follows the system locale by default; overridable in Settings (`spellCheckEnabled`, `spellCheckLanguage`). - Fenced code blocks and inline backtick spans are skipped via a `gtksourceview:context-classes:no-spell-check` tag maintained by `MarkdownNoSpellRanges`. - Cross-version C shim: builds against libspelling 0.2.0 (Ubuntu 24.04 LTS) where the type was `SpellingLanguageInfo`, and 0.4.x (Ubuntu 26.04+) where it was renamed to `SpellingLanguage`. - Packaging: `libspelling-1-dev` added to CI apt installs; `.deb` `Depends` includes `libspelling-1-1 | libspelling-1-2`. Flatpak and Snap pick it up from their GNOME runtimes. ## Tests / CI - 32 new tests across `NotesRepositoryFolderTests`, `SidebarTreeFlattenerTests`, `CLITests`, `RepositoryStateTests`, plus the spell-check `MarkdownNoSpellRangesTests`. Headless test count is 135. - New `MainWindowFolderActions` and `MainWindowSidebarDnD` extension files keep the new UI logic isolated. ## Notes for packagers - `.deb`: depends on `libspelling-1-1 | libspelling-1-2`. - `.rpm`: no spec change needed, `rpmbuild` autogenerates the SONAME requirement. - Flatpak / Snap: runtime ships libspelling-1. **Full Changelog**: https://github.com/makoni/swifty-notes-gtk/compare/1.1.3...1.1.4

## Highlights - **Snap launches cleanly on Ubuntu 26.04 and recent setups** (#11) — the previous Snap build aborted at startup with `AccessDenied: not allowed to own the service "me.spaceinbox.swiftynotes" due to AppArmor policy`. The Snap version now starts without that error under strict confinement. Tradeoff in the Snap build only: a second launch spawns a second process instead of focusing the running one. Flatpak and native installs keep the canonical single-instance behavior. - **Flatpak gains home-folder access** — you can now point Swifty Notes at any folder under your home directory, including cloud-synced ones like `~/Sync/Notes`, `~/Dropbox/Notes`, or `~/Documents/Notes`. Settings → Browse will now show the real path you picked instead of a synthetic portal mount path. After updating, your software centre may ask to confirm the new permission. - **Switching the notes folder is now atomic** (#13) — if a move fails partway through, your notes are restored to the original location instead of being left half-migrated. Reset works again from any state. - **Friendlier folder-change errors** (#13) — the "Could not change the notes folder" / "Could not open notes folder" dialog now shows user-facing text such as "Swifty Notes does not have permission to access that folder…" instead of bare `(NSCocoaErrorDomain error 512)`. - **Auto-recovery from stale notes-folder paths** — if a previously remembered notes folder no longer exists (for example a portal mount path inherited from an older Flatpak install), Swifty Notes now drops the dead reference on launch and falls back to the default folder, instead of erroring out on every operation. - **Insert Table icon now renders in standalone document windows** — previously the icon was missing when opening a single Markdown file in its own window. ## Under the hood - Internal refactor: `MainWindow` and `ExternalDocumentWindow` now share the formatting toolbar, preview-refresh debouncer, and editor↔preview scroll-sync helper. Future toolbar / preview tweaks apply to both windows automatically — the kind of drift that produced the missing-icon bug above can no longer happen. - Snap manifest minimised: `home` and `network` plugs only (no longer requesting `network-bind` or `removable-media`), matching the actual access patterns used by the markdown preview and notes folder. - Flathub manifest gains a `finish-args-home-filesystem-access` exception for `me.spaceinbox.swiftynotes`, so the new permission passes Flathub's lint. ## GitHub issues closed - #11 — [BUG] Cannot run 1.1.1 Snap - AppArmor policy restriction - #13 — Cannot move Notes folder **Full Changelog**: https://github.com/makoni/swifty-notes-gtk/compare/1.1.2...1.1.3

## Highlights - **Copy button on code blocks** (#9) — every fenced code block in the preview now shows a quick Copy button so you can grab a snippet in one click. - **Syntax highlighting in code blocks** (#7) — fenced blocks in the preview are now syntax-highlighted for popular languages, making longer snippets easier to scan. - **Insert Table button** (#6) — a new button in the formatting toolbar opens a visual grid picker, lets you set per-column alignment (Left / Center / Right), and drops a ready-to-edit Markdown table into the note. Remembers your last table size across sessions. - **Smarter formatting toolbar layout** (#5) — the toolbar now collapses to its compact layout based on its own measured content width, so buttons no longer disappear behind the header menu on narrower editor widths. - **Bundled formatting icons render everywhere** — the Table button and any future bundled formatting icons now render correctly on systems where the active icon theme doesn't ship a matching symbolic. ## Under the hood - Adopted `swift-adwaita` 1.2.4 APIs across the codebase and dropped direct `CAdwaita` imports — code is cleaner and ready for future framework updates. - Bumped `swift-adwaita` pin through 1.2.2 → 1.2.3 → 1.2.4 as the framework evolved. - Refactored to use `ApplicationFlags.handlesOpen` (`OptionSet`) instead of raw `GApplicationFlags` integers. **Full Changelog**: https://github.com/makoni/swifty-notes-gtk/compare/1.1.1...1.1.2

1.1.0 shipped a quiet regression: on many setups the file dialogs — Import into Library, Open Markdown File, Export, Save As, and Choose Notes Folder — never appeared when you triggered them. The click registered, the action fired, and then nothing happened. 1.1.1 is the fix release for that, plus a handful of related fixes and one small new feature that were ready to ship. ## Bug fixes - **File dialogs open reliably again.** Root cause was a `swift-adwaita` regression: the framework's 1.2.0 collapsed `FileDialog` onto async-only methods, and `Task { @MainActor in await dialog.open(…) }` bodies never run in a GTK application — Swift's `DispatchQueue.main` is not drained by the GLib main loop. Upstream `swift-adwaita` 1.2.1 restores the callback-based overloads, and Swifty Notes now uses `dialog.open(parent:) { result in … }` at every call-site (Import / Open / Export / Save As / Choose Notes Folder). ([#3](https://github.com/makoni/swifty-notes-gtk/issues/3), bump to `swift-adwaita` 1.2.1) - **Images attached to notes render in the preview again.** `PreviewImagePaintableLoader` used the same broken `Task { @MainActor in await Texture.load(…) }` pattern, so local `assets/…` images silently failed to load after app start. Replaced with synchronous `Texture(filename:)` (`gdk_texture_new_from_filename`) with a `picture.setFilename(…)` fallback for formats the GdkTexture fast path doesn't decode. No `async` between the click and the paintable being set. - **Paths with spaces no longer fail with "file not found".** In Swift 6, `URL.path()` returns a percent-encoded string (`%20` for space), but `FileManager.fileExists(atPath:)` / `attributesOfItem(atPath:)` want the decoded path. Every call-site that fed a user-chosen URL into `FileManager` was silently handing it an unresolvable string. Replaced each `.path()` with `.path(percentEncoded: false)` across `NotesRepository`, CLI, services, and UI. Library folders like `~/Cloud Disk/…` or `~/My Notes/…` now import, open, and export without errors. ([#3](https://github.com/makoni/swifty-notes-gtk/issues/3)) ## New - **Export notes together with their `assets/` folder.** ([#4](https://github.com/makoni/swifty-notes-gtk/issues/4)) `NotesRepository.export(note:to:assetsCollision:)` now also copies the note's local images into an `assets/` folder next to the destination Markdown. Collision policy is `.fail` (default) or `.merge`; the UI catches the fail case and offers **Cancel / Merge** in an alert. The toast reads "Exported <title> with N asset(s)" when a copy actually happened. Markdown references (`assets/pic.png`) stay untouched — they're already relative, so the exported bundle is self-contained out of the box. - **"New Window" in the dock / app-grid right-click menu.** The desktop entry now declares a `new-window` action. When Swifty Notes is already running (for example, with a standalone Markdown file open in an external-document window) you can right-click the icon and open a fresh notes library window without going through a terminal or relaunching. ## Dependencies - Bumped `swift-adwaita` pin to **1.2.1** (`ac066c64957b7fabb12b6d92289733bf3d3066e9`). The one reason is the restored callback `FileDialog` API. No source incompatibilities on our side — the async variants are still there, just unused in GTK-app code paths. ## Under the hood (non-user-facing) - Migrated 13 raw CAdwaita/GObject calls in `MarkdownPreviewWidgetTests` to high-level `swift-adwaita` 1.2.1 API (`Widget.sizeRequest`, `Widget.measure(orientation:forSize:)`, `Widget.tryCast`, `Widget.isInstance(of:)`). Nine `gtk_*` / `g_*` calls still remain — they'll migrate when `swift-adwaita` 1.2.2 ships the corresponding getters (`Widget.hasCSSClass`, `Picture.fileURL`/`.hasPaintable`, `Button.child`, `Box.orientation`, and overrides of `Button.gtkType` / `Box.gtkType`). - Hardened the pyatspi tree-walker in `UISmokeTests` against transient `None` children so `appCreatingNoteDoesNotEmitSnapshotWarningsUnderHeadlessWayland` no longer flakes in CI. - **Full Changelog**: https://github.com/makoni/swifty-notes-gtk/compare/1.1.0...1.1.1

## Highlights - Markdown preview now loads remote images, plays animated GIF/WebP, and handles inline badge rows. - Standalone HTML `` tags render as proper preview images. - Dialog call-sites migrated to the new async swift-adwaita API (swift-adwaita 1.2.0). ## Added - **Remote image loading in preview.** New `PreviewRemoteImageLoader` service fetches images by URL and hands a paintable back to the renderer. Loading is fully async on `MainActor` and cached per URL for the lifetime of the app. - **Animated image playback.** New `PreviewAnimatedImagePlayer` drives animated GIF and WebP frames through GTK's `Picture` widget using GdkPixbuf animation iterators. - **Image paintable sizing.** New `PreviewImagePaintableLoader` loads PNG/JPG/WebP via `Texture.load` and handles SVG/SVGZ via `Picture.setFilename`. SVG intrinsic dimensions are extracted from the file header so aspect ratios survive preferred-height scaling. - **Image group rendering.** New `RenderedBlock.imageGroup(items:)` case and `RenderedImageItem` model. The renderer detects a `

` that contains only linked images (CI badges, shields.io, etc.) and emits a single `imageGroup` block, which the preview lays out inline on one line with per-item `Button` link wrappers. - **Standalone HTML `` support.** `HTMLPreviewDocumentBuilder` now recognises a `

` whose only meaningful content is one or more `` / linked-`` elements and promotes them to `.image` or `.imageGroup` blocks instead of embedding them inside a paragraph. - **Scrollbar gizmo warning filter.** `ScrollbarGizmoWarningFilter` installs a `g_log_set_writer_func` that drops the harmless `"Trying to snapshot … without a current allocation"` warnings that leak out of internal scrolled-window children on GTK 4. ## Changed - **swift-adwaita bumped to 1.2.0.** Pulls in `isSame(as:)`, `emitClicked`, `emitSearchChanged`, `SplitButton.emitClicked`, `SimpleAction.activate`, `AppLauncher`, `Widget.gtkType`/`isInstance(of:)`, `Widget.sizeRequest`/`measure(orientation:forSize:)`, `Texture.load`, `Picture.intrinsicSize`, `Application.onOpen`, nonisolated `MainContext.idle`, and typed throws on the dialog APIs. - **Dialog call-sites migrated to the async API.** `MainWindowActionsAndFiles.importNote` / `openMarkdownFile` / `exportSelectedNote`, `ExternalDocumentWindow.saveDocumentAs`, and `SettingsWindow.chooseNotesFolder` now use the async `open`/`save`/`selectFolder` methods with typed-throws error handling. `Throwing` suffix dropped from call sites to match the framework rename. - **Preview refresh coordinator.** `MarkdownPreview` tracks `lastRefreshedPreviewWidth` and throttles block-image refreshes via a GLib timer, so sidebar/split-view width changes no longer re-fetch remote images on every allocation pass. ## Tests & CI - **Widget tests isolated into their own suite.** Moved `@MainActor` preview/widget tests out of `NoteModelAndRendererTests` into the new `MarkdownPreviewWidgetTests`. Running them in the same process as `MainWindow*Tests` left GLib idle callbacks referencing torn-down `GObject`s, which SIGSEGV'd the next test that pumped the main context. - **Dedicated CI step for widget tests.** `.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs `MarkdownPreviewWidgetTests` under its own `xvfb-run dbus-run-session` invocation, matching the core-tests pattern. - **WebP loader in CI.** Added `webp-pixbuf-loader` to the apt install list — without it `Texture.load` silently falls back and the remote WebP preview tests time out on GitHub runners. - **New coverage.** Tests for standalone HTML image blocks, linked badge image groups, async remote WebP/GIF loading, layout/sizing of images and badges, and `SwiftyNotesLauncherTests` hardened to prevent window presentation during document opening. `UISmokeTests` redirects application and Weston logs to `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`. **Full Changelog**: https://github.com/makoni/swifty-notes-gtk/compare/1.0.2...1.1.0

Swifty Notes 1.0.2 improves the split editor/preview layout and adds first-class support for opening and editing standalone Markdown files. ## Highlights - Added **Open Markdown File…** so you can open and edit standalone Markdown files without importing them into your notes library first. - Added desktop file association support so Swifty Notes can appear in **Open With** for Markdown files. - Improved narrow-window split view behavior so the preview can stay open more comfortably. - Made the formatting toolbar adaptive: it now switches into a compact icon-first presentation as space gets tighter. - Added a second fallback layout where the formatting toolbar can stack into two rows instead of clipping actions off-screen. ## Technical details - Introduced a dedicated external document window with in-place save, reload, **Save As…**, **Reveal in Folder**, and **Import into Library…** actions. - Routed desktop file-open requests into external document windows and reuse the existing window when the same file is opened again. - Moved the formatting toolbar into its own dedicated container so it no longer forces the editor pane to stay wider than necessary. - Reduced the editor pane minimum width in split view to let the preview expand further on smaller displays. - Added runtime layout switching for the toolbar: - full labels on wider layouts - compact icon-only buttons when the editor narrows - two-row compact layout when even the compact single-row toolbar would overflow - Added regression coverage for: - compact toolbar mode - two-row toolbar fallback - updated preview width resolution on tighter split layouts - external document open/save/reload behavior - launcher routing and window reuse for desktop-open requests **Full Changelog**: https://github.com/makoni/swifty-notes-gtk/compare/1.0.1...1.0.2

Swifty Notes 1.0.1 is a maintenance release focused on better CLI behavior for packaged installs, more consistent release/version metadata, and refreshed packaging inputs across Linux distribution formats. ## Highlights - **Better CLI experience for Flathub and other packaged installs** - Documented the correct packaged-install invocation: `flatpak run me.spaceinbox.swiftynotes cli ...` - Improved CLI notes-directory resolution so host-side CLI runs can discover notes stored in Flatpak-managed data when host storage is empty - Updated the in-app seeded CLI note and README so packaged-install guidance is consistent - **More consistent release and packaging metadata** - Centralized release version resolution around the repository `VERSION` file - Aligned version reporting and release metadata across runtime info, packaging scripts, and release automation - Updated AppStream release text for 1.0.1 and preserved 1.0.0 history in metainfo - **Packaging and dependency refresh** - Updated Snap packaging for the Swift 6.3 toolchain - Refreshed pinned source dependencies used by SwiftPM and Flatpak builds: - `swift-adwaita` -> `a9046505ba5c0adf7ab34d1fafa20837ec0d4e7e` - `swift-markdown` -> `55d66d9a9e8d4fd3f48d111b0d437e82fe451903` - `swift-cmark` -> `924936d0427cb25a61169739a7660230bffa6ea6` - Added minimum-version source dependency support where exact revision pinning no longer matched upstream package constraints - **Docs, storefront, and project presentation** - Added a Flathub download link to the README - Refreshed README feature text and screenshots - Added a GitHub sponsorship URL - **Reliability and regression coverage** - Added CLI regression tests covering default and configured Flatpak storage fallback - Improved Wayland UI smoke-test reliability with updated frame timing and app ID handling ## Technical details - Added `packaging/release/version.sh` and updated release scripts/workflows to resolve the release version from `VERSION` by default. - Updated `Sources/SwiftyNotes/CLI/NotesCLI.swift` with Flatpak-aware notes-directory resolution and clearer help text for packaged installs. - Updated `Sources/SwiftyNotes/Storage/SwiftyNotesCLISeed.swift`, `Sources/SwiftyNotes/Storage/SwiftyNotesOverviewSeed.swift`, and `README.md` so CLI usage guidance matches the packaged-install reality. - Refreshed `flatpak/me.spaceinbox.swiftynotes.yml.in`, `snap/snapcraft.yaml`, and related release scripts to keep packaging metadata aligned. - Preserved historical AppStream release history by keeping a static `1.0.0` entry below the current 1.0.1 release entry. **Full Changelog**: https://github.com/makoni/swifty-notes-gtk/compare/1.0.0...1.0.1
